paragraphs.source_en: Softly, I have gone, just as softly as I came. I softly waved farewell, bidding farewell to the cloud patterns in the western sky. The golden willows by the riverbank were a bride in the evening light. The vivid reflections in the rippling water swayed in the mirror of my heart. On soft mud, the green algae of the water, lush and smooth, swayed beneath the surface; in the tender currents of the Cam, I would gladly become a blade of watergrass. That pool under the shadow of the elm was no clear spring; it was the sky’s rainbow, broken apart among floating weeds and settling as a rainbow-like dream. Seeking a dream? I should pole a long staff, drifting upstream toward the greener reeds, load my boat with a harvest of starlight, and sing among the splendor of that starry sheen. But I cannot sing; hush is the clarion of farewell. Even the cicadas fall silent for me; silence is this night’s Camford Bridge. Quietly I have gone, just as quietly as I came. I flicked my sleeve once, carrying away not even a single wisp of cloud. November sixth, in China’s sea.

paragraphs.source_zh:
輕輕的我走了，

正如我輕輕的來；

我輕輕的招手，

作別西天的雲彩。

那河畔的金柳，

是夕陽中的新娘；

波光裏的豔影，

在我的心頭蕩漾。

輭泥
上
的靑荇，

油油的在水底招搖：

在康河的柔波裏，

我甘心做一條水草！

那楡蔭下的一潭，

不是淸泉，是天上虹

揉碎在浮藻間，

沈澱着彩虹似的夢。

尋夢？撑一支長篙，

向靑草更靑處漫溯，

滿載一船星輝，

在星輝斑斕裏放歌。

但我不能放歌，

悄悄是別離的笙簫；

夏蟲也爲我沈默，

沈默是今晚的康橋！

悄悄的我走了，

正如我悄悄的來；

我揮一揮衣袖，

不帶走一片雲彩。

十一月六日中國海上
